mechanism: CONFIRMED by execution, with the finding's 'reindex' half corrected. The hook is src/node/notify.lisp:20-28, a :updated-block-tip validation hook whose only guard is (not (chain-state-target-blockhash chainstate)) - i.e. it excludes an assumeutxo BACKGROUND chainstate and nothing else. There is no sync_state, no IBD test and no POST_INIT equivalent anywhere on the path. Core connects -blocknotify to uiInterface.NotifyBlockTip and the FIRST line of the lambda is `if (sync_state != SynchronizationState::POST_INIT) return;` (refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:2009-2018), where the state comes from GetSynchronizationState(still_in_ibd, blockfiles_indexed) (refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:3307-3312) and is INIT_DOWNLOAD during IBD, INIT_REINDEX while the block files are being re-indexed, POST_INIT otherwise. Core also fires blockTip ONCE per ActivateBestChain call, outside the connect do-while (refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:3452-3463), so a batch of connected blocks yields one notification. We fire it from TWO places: src/validation/block.lisp:2835, inside connect-block, i.e. once per CONNECTED BLOCK, and src/validation/block.lisp:4016, once per activate-best-chain step. The connect-block site is the one that matters: process-received-block reaches it at src/networking/protocol.lisp:931 (the network/IBD path) and activate-block reaches it at src/validation/block.lisp:4215 and :4289. The runner is run-notify-command (src/logging.lisp:567-586), which builds (list "/bin/sh" "-c" cmd) and calls uiop:launch-program detached. The hook is armed at src/node/init.lisp:153-156, before any sync work, so it is live for the whole of a from-scratch sync. CORRECTION to the finding: our -reindex (src/node/init.lisp:673-682) rebuilds only the BLOCK INDEX from the block files and does not re-connect bodies, and -reindex-chainstate (src/node/reindex.lisp:3) replays UTXO effects directly without touching connect-block or the hook, so neither reindex mode is itself a fork storm; the subsequent re-activation goes through activate-best-chain, which fires once per +activation-step-blocks+ = 1000 blocks. The exposure is the network sync path, not reindex.
consequence: REAL, S2. Executed: with *block-notify-command* set to a real shell command and 200 regtest blocks connected through the shipped connect-block path, the hook ran exactly 200 times - one /bin/sh fork+exec per connected block, per-block ratio exactly 1, with bl.net:*cached-is-ibd* still T and chain-state-target-blockhash NIL, so the one guard that exists did not fire. A 1000-block regtest IBD therefore spawns 1000 detached /bin/sh; extrapolated at the same 1:1 ratio a testnet4 sync is on the order of 90,000 spawns and a mainnet sync on the order of 900,000, against Core's ZERO for the same sync. That is a self-inflicted fork storm an operator reaches with a documented, standard option - -blocknotify is the ordinary wiring for a block explorer, a mining backend or a monitor - which is exactly the S2 shape (an operator can hit it with a documented option). The secondary effect is arguably worse than the CPU: every one of those invocations is a spurious 'new best block' signal to whatever the hook drives, so an explorer reindexes or a pool refreshes work hundreds of thousands of times during a sync that Core would have kept silent. BOUNDING WORK, which is why this is not S1: the spawns do NOT accumulate. After the 200-spawn run the container held 5 processes and ZERO in state Z (checked by reading /proc/*/stat), so SBCL reaps the detached children and there is no pid-table exhaustion; the cost is sustained fork/exec churn and the downstream signal flood, not unbounded resource growth. run-notify-command also never signals (handler-case around the launch), so a failing or missing hook cannot break block connection. And the drive site at src/validation/block.lisp:4016 is not part of the problem: at one notification per 1000-block step it is more conservative than Core, not less.
evidence: Executed in the pinned project container (bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4) through cl-workbench repl eval. Probe: (with-network (:regtest)) + make-activate-block-fixture + build-and-connect over 200 chain hashes, with bl::*block-notify-command* bound to "printf 'x' >> /tmp/<tag>.txt", then the file length read back after a settle. Result: (:BLOCKS 200 :SPAWNS 200 :PER-BLOCK 1 :NOTIFY-COMMAND-SET T :IBD-LATCHED T :CS-TARGET-BLOCKHASH NIL). Zombie check inside the container after the run: process count 5, processes in state Z: 0. Activation step size read from the image: (:STEP-BLOCKS 1000) for bitcoin-lisp.validation::+activation-step-blocks+ (src/validation/block.lisp:3896). Ours: src/node/notify.lisp:11-28 (the defvar and the hook, with its single target-blockhash guard); src/validation/block.lisp:2835 (per-connected-block), :4016 (per activation step), :3930-3990 (activate-best-chain), :4215 and :4289 (activate-block's two connect-block calls); src/networking/protocol.lisp:931 (process-received-block's connect); src/logging.lisp:567-586 (run-notify-command, uiop:launch-program detached); src/node/init.lisp:153-156 (the hook armed before sync), :673-682 (-reindex is index-only); src/node/reindex.lisp:3-60 (-reindex-chainstate replays UTXO effects, no hook); src/config-options.lisp:62-63. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:2009-2018 (the POST_INIT gate) and :498 (the option); refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:3307-3312 (GetSynchronizationState) and :3452-3463 (blockTip once per ActivateBestChain, outside the connect loop); refs/bitcoin/src/node/kernel_notifications.cpp:51-60.
fix_shape: Give the hook Core's gate at the hook, not at the drive site, so every future subscriber of :updated-block-tip can make the same distinction. Carry a synchronization state alongside the notification the way Core's blockTip does: notify-updated-block-tip (src/util/validation-interface.lisp:79) should take a state argument computed by our equivalent of GetSynchronizationState - :post-init unless the node is in initial block download or is rebuilding the block index, in which case :init-download / :init-reindex - and notify-block-tip should return immediately unless the state is :post-init, which is a literal transcription of init.cpp:2012. The IBD predicate already exists (bl.net:initial-block-download-p / *cached-is-ibd*, src/networking/protocol.lisp:647-690); the reindex flag needs to be readable at the notification site, so thread it from the -reindex handling in init rather than inferring it. While there, close the second divergence: Core notifies once per ActivateBestChain call after the whole connect loop, so the announcement belongs after the batch, not inside connect-block - moving the src/validation/block.lisp:2835 call to the callers that complete an activation (activate-block's two arms and activate-best-chain's step end, which already announces at :4016) makes a multi-block catch-up produce one notification, as Core does, and leaves the steady-state one-block case unchanged. Note that the same hook list also drives -stopatheight and the periodic flush, so the state argument must be advisory to subscribers rather than a filter on the announcement itself, or -stopatheight stops working during IBD. Tests: connect N blocks with the node in IBD and assert the hook ran zero times; leave IBD and assert one run per activation; a positive control that the hook DOES fire post-init, so the assertion cannot pass because the plumbing is dead.
